# Your Person NZ

> Your Person NZ is a local coordination and concierge service for New Zealanders living overseas who have a parent or family member living independently in Christchurch and Canterbury, New Zealand. It is not an aged-care, nursing, medical or personal-care provider. It coordinates practical, everyday local support — trades, house checks, errands, appointments and similar — through appropriate third-party providers, who generally quote and invoice the family directly.

## Who it's for

New Zealanders aged roughly 40–65 living overseas (commonly Australia, the UK, Singapore, the US or Canada) who have a parent or family member aged roughly 70+ still living independently in Christchurch or wider Canterbury. The parent is typically autonomous and independent, not requiring aged care.

## What it does

- Coordinates trades, repairs, appointments, gardening, cleaning and similar practical jobs
- Arranges someone trustworthy to be physically present when needed (e.g. for a tradesperson visit)
- Checks the house or a completed job and reports back honestly
- Sources and vets local tradespeople and services in Christchurch and Canterbury
- Keeps the overseas family updated in plain language, with photos where relevant
- Is exploring door-to-door travel companion support for independent older travellers visiting family overseas

## What it does not do

- Does not provide nursing, personal care, medical care or aged residential care
- Does not provide financial management or legal advice
- Is not an emergency response service — for medical, police or fire emergencies, contact New Zealand emergency services on 111
- Does not take over decision-making from the family; it works with families, not around them

## Service area

Christchurch and wider Canterbury, New Zealand (pilot phase, as of 2026). The customer/family can live anywhere in the world. Not yet available in other regions of New Zealand.

## Pricing

Ongoing local support is expected to start from around NZ$199–299/month during the founding family pilot; one-off support and larger projects are priced separately. Third-party trades and services are generally paid directly by the family. Pricing is indicative during the pilot.
